## 8. Headless (`-n`) stdout rules

Without any `-c`/`-f`, headless mode dumps the current top view to stdout at exit:
- file args: the loaded lines (multiple files interleaved by timestamp);
- piped stdin: the piped bytes (timestamp-prefixed if `-t`);
- `-e`: the captured command output (file args given together with `-e` were NOT dumped —
  the exec-output view wins; with two `-e`s only the last output was dumped);
- binary files: a hex dump (`     File Offset  00 01 ...` header, `┌─`/`─│` box-drawing
  in the ASCII gutter);
- nothing loaded: nothing (with `-N`), or the "nothing to do" error (without `-N`).

When `-c`/`-f` commands are present, the dump is of whatever the commands leave behind;
observed matrix (all exit 0):

| commands | stdout |
|---|---|
| `-c ';SELECT 1 AS one'` | `   one     \n         1 \n` (table; header + value, space-padded; exact bytes `   one     \n         1 \n`) |
| `-c ';SELECT 1 AS a' -c ';SELECT 2 AS b'` | only the LAST table (`    b      \n         2 \n`) |
| `-c ':echo A' -c ':echo B'` | `A\nB\n` (both, in order) |
| any mix containing `:echo` (e.g. `;sql` then `:echo`, `:echo` then `;sql`, `;sql,:echo,;sql`) | only the `:echo` texts, in order; SQL tables never appear |
| `-q` anywhere | suppresses the view dump entirely (incl. SQL tables and file dumps); `:echo` output still printed |

(The exact mechanism for the `:echo`/SQL interaction is ambiguous; above is purely empirical.)

## 10. Exit-code summary

| Code | Trigger |
|---|---|
| 0 | success; `-h`/`-V`/`-H`; `-u`; `-i` ok; `-W` (even with warnings); runtime command errors in `-c`/`-f`; child `-e` failures; TUI init failure on a real TTY |
| 1 | runtime errors: "nothing to do", file open failure, invalid `--since/--until`, file outside time cutoffs, `-i` unreadable file, `-m` operation errors, stdout-not-a-TTY |
| 105 | option value validation: `-I` bad dir/file, `-c` empty or missing `:`/`;`/`\|` prefix |
| 107 | `-i` without a file (`-i requires file`) |
| 108 | exclusion: `-i` with `-n`/`-N`/`-c` (`-i excludes -n` etc.) |
| 109 | unexpected argument (unknown flag, extra positional, flag not allowed in `-m` mode) |
| 114 | arity: missing option argument (`1 required ... missing`), option given too many times (`At Most 1 required but received 2`) |

## 2. `-V` / `--version`

- Exact output: `lnav 0.14.0-07efb63\n` to **stdout**, exit **0**.
- `-V` is effectively pre-scanned: it wins over almost everything:

  - `-h -V`, `-hV`, `-Vh` → version only (help NOT printed). `-V` beats `-h`.

  exit 114, `reason: -d: 1 required FILE missing` (no version printed).

## 3. Help/version pre-scan vs. parse errors (ordering)

Observed precedence (highest first):

1. Missing / excess option arguments → exit **114** (beats `-h`/`-V`).
2. `-V` → version, exit 0 (beats `-h`, unknown flags, exclusions, management mode).
3. `-h`/`--help` → help to stderr, exit 0 (beats unknown flags: `-h -Z`, `-Z -h`,
   `--help -Z`, `-h foo` all print help, exit 0).
4. Unknown/unexpected arguments → exit **109**.
5. Exclusion violations (`-i` vs `-n`/`-N`/`-c`) → exit **108**.
6. Value validation (`-I` not a dir, `-c` empty/bad prefix) → exit **105**.
7. `-i` with no file → exit **107**.
8. Runtime errors (file open, time parse, TUI, "nothing to do") → exit **1**.

Caveat: `-h`/`-V` do not rescue you from an option that *consumes* them as its argument:
`-c -h` runs with cmd `-h` → exit 105; `-S -h` parses `-h` as a time → exit 1.

## 5. Option syntax details

- Short-option bundling works: `-nq`, `-hV`, `-nZq` (bundle parse stops at the unknown
  member; error reports the rest, e.g. `-Zq`).
- Attached short-option args work: `-c:echo\ hi`, `-c;SELECT 42`, `-dfile.log` style
  (verified for `-c`).
- Long options accept both `--since VALUE` and `--since=VALUE`.
- No long-option abbreviations: `--sinc`, `--vers` → exit 109.
- `--` terminates option parsing; following tokens are files even if they start with `-`
  (tested `-- -h`, `-- -weird.log`, `-- --strange.log` — all treated as file names).
- A lone `-` is a positional meaning "stdin" (`printf 'via dash\n' | lnav -n -` works;
  with empty stdin it yields the "nothing to do" error, exit 1).
- Repeatable: `-c`, `-e`, `-f`, `-I` (multi-use OK, executed/used in order);
  boolean flags (`-n -N -q -t -r -R -W -u`) repeat silently.
- NOT repeatable: `-d`, `-S`/`-U` ("At Most 1", exit 114). `-i` consumes all following
  positionals as files (its "repeat" test actually errored on `-N` exclusion).
- `-i` excludes `-n`, `-N`, `-c` (exit 108) but allows `-q`, `-d`, `-I`, `-W`.
- `-m` rejects `-n`, `-N`, `-c`, `-W` as "not expected" (exit 109); allows `-q`, `-d`, `-I`.
- `-u` is compatible with `-N`, `-q`, `-c`, `-i` (in `-i f -u`, the `-u` message printed
  and the install did not run; exit 0).

## 6. Meta flags

### `-d file` (debug log)
- Creates `file` mode **0640** (`-rw-r-----`), subject to umask; **appends** across runs
  (each run adds a `lnav started 1` record + `arg[N] = ...` lines).
- Unwritable path (e.g. nonexistent directory): **silently ignored**, exit 0, no message.
- Not created at all when argument parsing fails (`-d dbg.log -Z` → exit 109, no file).
- Line format: `2026-08-08T19:46:51.580329+00:00 E t0 lnav.cc:2821 unable to set locale to ''`
  (ISO-8601 µs timestamp, level letter E/W/I/D, thread `t0`, source `file:line`, message).
  A trivial `-n -N` run produced ~3,654 lines.
- With no locale env: logs `E ... unable to set locale to ''`; with `LANG=C.UTF-8` that
  line disappears. This box always logs `failed to setup tz: discover_tz_dir failed to
  find zoneinfo` (no `/usr/share/zoneinfo`); `TZ=...` does not help.

### `-N`
- Skips default-file loading: `-n -N </dev/null` → exit 0, total silence.
- Also suppresses the implicit reading of piped stdin:
  `printf 'x\n' | lnav -n` prints `x`, but `printf 'x\n' | lnav -N -n` prints nothing.
- With explicit file args, `-N` is a no-op (files load normally).

### `-q`
- Does NOT suppress errors, `-W` warnings, `-i` messages, `-u` message, or `:echo` output.
- In headless mode it suppresses the default end-of-run **dump of the current view**:
  - `lnav -n f.log` prints the file's lines; `lnav -q -n f.log` prints nothing (exit 0).
  - `printf 'q1\n' | lnav -q -n` prints nothing.
  - `lnav -q -n -e 'echo eq'` prints nothing; `lnav -q -n -c ';SELECT 9 AS nine' -N` prints nothing.
  - `lnav -q -n -c ':echo hi-q' -N` still prints `hi-q` (`:echo` writes directly to stdout).

### `-W`
- Prints configuration warnings to **stderr**, exit 0. With the broken
  `formats/installed/badfmt.json` present, exact output (651 bytes):

```
  warning: unexpected value for property “/myfmt/regex/std”
 --> /opt/uiuc-agent/home/.lnav/formats/installed/badfmt.json:1
 | {"myfmt":{"regex":{"std":"^(?<timestamp>[0-9]+(((($"},"sample":[{"line":"123"}]}}
 =   help: Available Properties
           ([^/]+)/
  warning: format file is missing “$schema” property
 --> /opt/uiuc-agent/home/.lnav/formats/installed/badfmt.json
 =   note: the schema specifies the supported format version and can be used with editors to automatically validate the file
 =   help: add the following property to the top-level JSON object:
             "$schema": "https://lnav.org/schemas/format-v1.schema.json",
```
- Without `-W`, these warnings are completely hidden in normal mode (but the same broken

### `-u`
- With no git-installed formats: prints to **stdout**
  `No formats from git repositories found, use 'lnav -i extra' to install third-party formats`

### `-I dir`
- Extra config dir; must exist and be a directory (else exit 105, see table).
- Valid dir: silently accepted. Repeatable.

### `-H`
- Dumps the entire internal help (all commands, SQL functions, etc.) to **stdout**:
  260,148 bytes with `-n`, exit 0, stderr empty. Starts with `\nlnav 0.14.0\n\nA fancy

## 7. Loading flags (`-c`, `-f`, `-e`, `-t`, `-r`, `-R`, `-S`/`-U`)

- `-c cmd`: cmd must start with `:` (lnav command), `;` (SQL), or `|` (script), else the
  exit-105 snippet error above. Multiple `-c` execute in argv order; `-c` and `-f`
  interleave in argv order (`-c ':echo c1' -c ':echo c2' -f cmds.lnav` printed
  `c1`, `c2`, `from-file`).
- A failing `-c` command does NOT change the exit code: `-c ':nosuchcmd'` → exit **0**
  with `  error: unknown command: “nosuchcmd”` on stderr. SQL errors similarly: exit 0,

```

 reason: no such table: nonexistent
 --> command-option:1
 | SELECT bogus_col FROM nonexistent       ␣(padded)
```
- `-f file`: nonexistent script → exit **0**(!) with

```
  error: unknown script -- /no/such/file.lnav -- file not found
 --> command-option:1
 | |/no/such/file.lnav                     ␣(padded)
```
- `-e cmd`: runs `cmd` via `/bin/bash -c` (error text was `/bin/bash: line 1: nosuchcmd123:
  command not found`). Child stdout AND stderr are merged into one captured stream.
  Child exit status is ignored (`-e 'exit 3'` → lnav exit 0). With multiple `-e`, only
  the last one's output ended up in the final view.
- `-t`: piped stdin lines that lack timestamps get one prepended in format
  `2026-08-08T19:45:31.557007+0000 ` (ISO-8601, microseconds, `+0000` — note no colon in
  the zone). Without `-t`, stdin lines pass through unchanged in the dump.
- `-S/--since`, `-U/--until`: filter by time; both orders and `=` form work.
  Bad values → exit 1, e.g.
  `  error: invalid 'since' time “-h”` / ` reason: Unrecognized input`, or
  `  error: invalid 'since' time “2024-13-45 99:99”` / ` reason: No time unit given for the previous number`.
  A file entirely outside the cutoff → exit 1:

```
  error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/cli/times.log
 reason: file contents are out-of-range of time cutoffs “/tmp/probe/cli/times.log”
 |        = note: File time range is “2026-08-08 19:50:34.000000” to “2026-08-08 19:50:34.000000”
 |        = note: Minimum time cutoff is “2026-08-08 19:00:00.000000”
```
- `-r`, `-R`: accepted; no observable output difference in the small tests.

---

## 8. Headless (`-n`) stdout rules

Without any `-c`/`-f`, headless mode dumps the current top view to stdout at exit:
- file args: the loaded lines (multiple files interleaved by timestamp);
- piped stdin: the piped bytes (timestamp-prefixed if `-t`);
- `-e`: the captured command output (file args given together with `-e` were NOT dumped —
  the exec-output view wins; with two `-e`s only the last output was dumped);
- binary files: a hex dump (`     File Offset  00 01 ...` header, `┌─`/`─│` box-drawing
  in the ASCII gutter);
- nothing loaded: nothing (with `-N`), or the "nothing to do" error (without `-N`).

When `-c`/`-f` commands are present, the dump is of whatever the commands leave behind;
observed matrix (all exit 0):

| commands | stdout |
|---|---|
| `-c ';SELECT 1 AS one'` | `   one     \n         1 \n` (table; header + value, space-padded; exact bytes `   one     \n         1 \n`) |
| `-c ';SELECT 1 AS a' -c ';SELECT 2 AS b'` | only the LAST table (`    b      \n         2 \n`) |
| `-c ':echo A' -c ':echo B'` | `A\nB\n` (both, in order) |
| any mix containing `:echo` (e.g. `;sql` then `:echo`, `:echo` then `;sql`, `;sql,:echo,;sql`) | only the `:echo` texts, in order; SQL tables never appear |
| `-q` anywhere | suppresses the view dump entirely (incl. SQL tables and file dumps); `:echo` output still printed |

(The exact mechanism for the `:echo`/SQL interaction is ambiguous; above is purely empirical.)

---

## 9. stdin / stdout / TTY matrix

| setup | result |
|---|---|
| no `-n`, stdout not a TTY (regardless of stdin: /dev/null, closed, pipe with data, `-t`) | exit **1**, stderr: `  error: unable to display interactive text UI` / ` reason: stdout is not a TTY` / ` = help: pass the -n option to run lnav in headless mode or don't redirect stdout` |
| `-n -N`, stdin /dev/null / closed (`0<&-`) / empty pipe | exit 0, no output |
| `-n` (no `-N`), stdin /dev/null or empty pipe | exit **1**: `  error: nothing to do` / ` reason: no files given or default files found` / ` = help: use the “-N” option to open lnav without loading any files` (there is no `/var/log/syslog` on this box) |
| `-n`, stdin pipe with data | data auto-loaded as a file, dumped to stdout, exit 0 |
| `-N -n`, stdin pipe with data | stdin ignored, exit 0, no output |
| `-n f.log`, stdin pipe with data | stdin ignored, file dumped |
| `-n -` with data | loads stdin explicitly |
| stdout = TTY (pty), any TERM tried (`xterm`, `xterm-256color`, `linux`, `vt100`, `dumb`, unset) | TUI fails on this box; sequence: enter alt screen `\e[?1049h`, terminal queries (`\e[6n`, `\e[>u`, `\e[=27u`, `\e[=c`, `\e[>0q`, DCS `+q544e;524742;687061`, 256× OSC-4 color queries, ...), then leave alt screen `\e[?1049l` and print to the tty: `  error: unable to open TUI\r\n reason: unable to initialize notcurses No such file or directory\r\n = help: The TERM value of “<TERM>” is not known.  Check for your terminal in https://github.com/dankamongmen/notcurses/blob/master/TERMINALS.md or use “xterm-256color”\r\n` — **exit code 0 despite the error**. With TERM unset: reason becomes `Inappropriate ioctl for device` and help says `The TERM environment variable is not set.` |

So: interactive mode requires stdout to be a TTY *and* a working notcurses/terminfo;
the first check fails with exit 1, the second (surprisingly) exits 0.

---

## 10. Exit-code summary

| Code | Trigger |
|---|---|
| 0 | success; `-h`/`-V`/`-H`; `-u`; `-i` ok; `-W` (even with warnings); runtime command errors in `-c`/`-f`; child `-e` failures; TUI init failure on a real TTY |
| 1 | runtime errors: "nothing to do", file open failure, invalid `--since/--until`, file outside time cutoffs, `-i` unreadable file, `-m` operation errors, stdout-not-a-TTY |
| 105 | option value validation: `-I` bad dir/file, `-c` empty or missing `:`/`;`/`\|` prefix |
| 107 | `-i` without a file (`-i requires file`) |
| 108 | exclusion: `-i` with `-n`/`-N`/`-c` (`-i excludes -n` etc.) |
| 109 | unexpected argument (unknown flag, extra positional, flag not allowed in `-m` mode) |
| 114 | arity: missing option argument (`1 required ... missing`), option given too many times (`At Most 1 required but received 2`) |

---

## 11. Environment & file-system side effects

- **HOME**: state root is `$HOME/.lnav`. On first run with a fresh HOME, lnav creates
  (all dirs mode **0750**): `.lnav/configs/default/` (16 `*.json.sample` theme/keymap
  files), `.lnav/configs/installed/` (empty), `.lnav/crash/`, `.lnav/staging/`,
  `.lnav/formats/default/` (≈95 files: `*.json.sample` formats, `*.lnav` scripts,
  a few `.py`/`.sh`/`.sql`), `.lnav/formats/installed/` (empty). 113 files total;
  sample files are mode **0600**. No `config.json` or session DB is written by a
  bare `-n -N` run. `-V`/`-h` alone do not create anything.
- **HOME unset or empty**: lnav silently uses the **current working directory** as the
  state root — it creates `crash/`, `staging/`, `configs/`, `formats/` directly in cwd
  (no `.lnav` component), and `-h` prints the cwd as the config path. Exit 0.
- **Work dir**: `/tmp/lnav-user-0-work` (uid-based name) is NOT created by `-h`/`-V` or
  `-n -N`; it appears (mode 0750, with `piper/p-<hash>-000/out.<hash>.1` inside) only
  when piped stdin is actually captured. (`archives/` was also seen there after other runs.)
- **TERM**: only matters for the TUI (see §9); headless operation is TERM-independent.
- **LANG/LC_\***: unset locale only produces a debug-log error line; behavior unchanged.
- **TZ**: ignored for zone setup (no zoneinfo DB on this box); timestamps in output use
  `+0000`.
- **LNAV_HOME**: no effect (help still showed `$HOME/.lnav`; no directory created).

args.command:
cat > /workspace/notes/05-files.md <<'REPORT_EOF'
# lnav 0.14.0 — File Loading Mechanics (Area 05)

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`lnav 0.14.0-07efb63`). All probes done by running the
binary headless (`-n`) and capturing stdout/stderr/exit codes byte-for-byte.
Scratch dir `/tmp/probe`; `$HOME` redirected to `/tmp/probe/home2` for most runs
(lnav writes state to `$HOME/.lnav`; extraction/work files go to `/tmp/lnav-user-0-work`).

Baseline test file `app.log` (169 bytes, 4 lines, LF-terminated):
```
2024-01-15 10:00:01.000 INFO starting up
2024-01-15 10:00:02.000 WARN something odd
2024-01-15 10:00:03.000 ERROR failure happened
2024-01-15 10:00:04.000 INFO all done
```
Note: this timestamp format is NOT a known log format to lnav — its debug log says
`file does not have a known text format` and `setting text format to text/plain`, yet the
leading timestamps are still recognized for time-sorting (generic timestamp detection).

---

## 1. Baseline headless behavior

- `/workspace/executable -n app.log` → stdout is the file content byte-for-byte (no ANSI
  escapes, no headers), stderr empty, exit 0.
- A file whose last line lacks a trailing newline gets one appended in output
  (`printf 'no trailing newline text' > f` → output ends `text\n`).
- `-q` suppresses the log dump entirely (stdout 0 bytes, exit 0).
- Empty file (0 bytes): exit 0, stdout 0 bytes, stderr empty.
- Any single-file open failure aborts the whole run: `lnav -n app.log /nope.log` →
  stdout EMPTY (nothing dumped), stderr error, exit 1.

## 2. Multiple files: timestamp merge & tie-breaking

- Two log files given in either argument order are merged strictly by parsed timestamp:
  arg order `(app.log other.log)` and `(other.log app.log)` produce identical, time-sorted
  output.
- Equal timestamps across files: ties are broken by file path (lexicographic), NOT by
  argument order. Args `(zzz.log aaa.log)` still print aaa.log's line first. Same result
  when both files have identical mtime.
- Cross-format merge works: a syslog-format file (`Jan 15 09:15:00 myhost sshd[123]: ...`)
  merges by time with the `2026-01-15 ...` file. Syslog lines with no year were treated as
  year 2026 (file mtime year — file was created 2026-08; current date also 2026).
- Exception (multi-member gzip, see §4): content from concatenated gzip members is NOT
  time-merged across the member boundary.

## 3. View-selection rules in headless mode (what actually gets printed)

Empirical matrix:

| Inputs | Printed |
|---|---|
| one log file | its lines |
| several log files | all, time-merged |
| one plain-text file (no timestamps) | its lines |
| two plain-text files | ONLY the last one on the command line |
| log file(s) + text file(s) (any order) | ONLY the log lines; text hidden |
| log file + `-e` exec output (timestamped) | ONLY the log file; exec output hidden |
| file args + implicit piped stdin (timestamped) | ONLY the files; stdin silently ignored |
| `-e` cmd + piped stdin | ONLY exec output; stdin ignored |
| `-` (explicit stdin) + file args | BOTH, time-merged |

I.e. headless mode prints one "top" view: the merged log view if any real log files were
loaded; otherwise a single text/exec/stdin source (the last one wins).

## 4. Compressed files

Supported, transparently decompressed, output identical to the original (verified with
`cmp`), exit 0, stderr empty:

- **gzip** (`.gz`), **bzip2** (`.bz2`), **xz** (`.xz`), **zstd** (`.zst`; tested with a
  hand-crafted valid raw-block zstd frame since no zstd CLI existed — lnav decoded it).
- Detection is by **content magic bytes, not extension**: a gzip stream in a file named
  `noext_gz` is decompressed; plain text named `fake.gz` is passed through as text with no
  error; plain text named `bad.gz` passes through.
- **Truncated gzip** (first 60 bytes of a .gz): partial decompressed content is emitted
  (ending mid-line, no newline added after the partial fragment), NO error, exit 0.
- **Multi-member gzip** (`gzip -c a > mm.gz; gzip -c b >> mm.gz`): both members decoded,
  but output is member1's lines then member2's lines — NOT time-merged across members.
- **gzip on stdin** is also detected and decompressed.
- Compressed files inside directories (arg or `-r` scan) are decompressed too.
- Extraction cache: for `.bz2`/`.xz`/`.zst` (and archives), lnav creates
  `/tmp/lnav-user-0-work/archives/arc-<32hex>-<basename>/` containing the decompressed
  payload (mode `-r--------`), plus sidecar files `….done` and `….lck` (0 bytes, mode
  `-rw-------`). Plain `.gz` files did not get an `arc-` dir (streamed inline).
  The hash directory name changes when file content changes. These dirs persist after exit.

## 5. Rotated logs and `-R`

Given a base file arg, `-R` also loads sibling files matching rotation patterns.
Observed included: `svc.log.0`, `svc.log.1`, `svc.log.2`, `svc.log.2.gz`, `y.log.1.bz2`,
`y.log.2.xz`, `y.log.3.zst`, `y.log.10`, `x.log.20240114`, `x.log.old`.
Observed NOT included: `x.log-2024-01-14` (dash-date style), `ylog.1` (different base).
All loaded rotations are time-merged with the base. Without `-R`, only the named file is
loaded.

- Directory args load ALL top-level files regardless of `-R` (rotation-looking files
  included either way) — `-R` only matters for explicit file args.
- `-R` with a `.gz` base (`lnav -R app.log.gz`) FAILS: it globs `app.log.gz.*`, finds
  nothing, exit 1, stderr:
```
  error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/app.log.gz.*
 reason: failed to find path of “/tmp/probe/app.log.gz.*”
 |        reason: No such file or directory
```
- Content-based dedup applies to rotations: when `svc.log.2.gz` held an exact copy of
  `svc.log.1`'s content, its lines were NOT duplicated in output.

## 6. Duplicate detection

- Same file twice (`lnav app.log app.log`), two copies with different names
  (`app.log appcopy.log`), plain+gzip of same content, symlink+target — all loaded ONCE.
- Debug log (`-d`) shows: `Keeping duplicated file: 9e3e94ae9b1134c0105ae4512b071a0c;
  size=169; mtime=1786218262; path=/tmp/probe/app.log` (32-hex content hash).

## 7. Directories as args

- `lnav dir` loads every non-hidden regular file directly inside (non-recursive),
  decompression included; files are time-merged.
- `lnav -r dir` recurses into subdirectories (any depth).
- Dotfiles inside a scanned directory are SKIPPED (`dir/.secret.log` not loaded), but a
  dotfile passed explicitly as an arg loads fine.
- A FIFO inside a scanned directory is silently skipped.
- A directory containing only subdirectories, without `-r`: exit 0, no output, no error.
- An EMPTY directory is a hard error (it globs `dir/*` and fails), exit 1, stderr:
```
  error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/emptydir/*
 reason: failed to find path of “/tmp/probe/emptydir/*”
 |        reason: No such file or directory
```
- Symlink to a directory: followed, treated as a directory.
- Trailing slash on a directory is fine. Trailing slash on a FILE → exit 1:
```
  error: unable to open file: app.log/
 reason: Not a directory
```
- Glob patterns are expanded by lnav itself: quoted arg `'rot3/y.log.*'` loads all matches
  (base file itself not matched by the pattern is not loaded).
- `-r` with plain file args is harmless (files load normally).
- `--` separator works normally.

## 8. Special files

- Symlink to file: followed transparently.
- Broken symlink: exit 1, stderr:
```
  error: unable to open file: broken.log
 reason: No such file or directory
```
- FIFO as explicit arg: blocks reading until writer closes, then dumps content, exit 0
  (tested with a background writer).
- Unix domain socket as arg: exit 1, stderr:
```
  error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/sock
 reason: failed to open required file “/tmp/probe/sock”
 |        reason: Invalid argument
```
- Unreadable file (`chmod 000`): when running as root it still reads. As user `nobody`
  (via setpriv): exit 1, stderr:
```
  error: file exists, but is not readable: /tmp/probe/appcopy.log
 reason: Permission denied
```
- Nonexistent path: exit 1, stderr:
```
  error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/does-not-exist.log
 reason: No such file or directory
```

## 9. Standard input

- `echo ... | lnav -n` (no file args): stdin content is loaded and dumped, exit 0.
  Requires non-empty stdin: `lnav -n < /dev/null` or `printf '' | lnav -n` → exit 1:
```
  error: nothing to do
 reason: no files given or default files found
 = help: use the “-N” option to open lnav without loading any files
```
- `-N` with no files: exit 0, no output.
- Implicit stdin is IGNORED when file args are present (even timestamped stdin lines do
  not appear). Use `-` as an explicit arg to merge stdin with files (time-merged).
- `-t`: prepends the current wall-clock timestamp to each stdin line, format

## 13. Binary / invalid-UTF-8 handling

Two distinct renderings:

### a) Whole-file hexdump ("binary" files)
Triggered for heavily-invalid content (e.g. 512 bytes of /dev/urandom, truncated tar).
Exact format (from a file containing bytes 0x00..0xff):

Header line (note leading 5 spaces and trailing spaces):
```
     File Offset  00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07  08 09 0a 0b 0c 0d 0e 0f        ASCII      
```
Data rows: offset lowercase-hex right-aligned in 16 columns, two spaces, 16 hex bytes
(`%02x` lowercase, space-separated, double space between byte 7 and 8), two spaces, then a
16-glyph ASCII column. Last row is space-padded to full width. Glyph map in ASCII column
(verified for every byte value 0x00–0xff):
- `0x00` → `⋄` (U+22C4, bytes E2 8B 84)
- `0x01–0x08`, `0x0e–0x1f`, `0x7f` → `•` (U+2022, E2 80 A2)
- `0x09–0x0d` (tab, LF, VT, FF, CR) and `0x20` (space) → `_`
- `0x21–0x7e` → literal ASCII
- `0x80–0xff` → `×` (U+00D7, C3 97)

### b) Text view with per-line annotation
If the file is mostly text but its FIRST line contains invalid UTF-8 (including NUL), the
raw line is emitted VERBATIM (NUL/0xff bytes included), followed by a note and a hexdump
of just that line:
```
line one\0line two
 Line 1 at file offset 0 contains invalid UTF-8 content, the following is a hex dump of the line
 6c 69 6e 65 20 6f 6e 65  00 6c 69 6e 65 20 74 77  line_one⋄line_tw
 6f                                                o
```
(1 leading space on note/hexdump lines; same glyph map as above.) Only line 1 is
annotated — invalid bytes in later lines pass through raw with no note.

### Detection threshold (empirical, approximate)
- Valid UTF-8 control bytes (0x01–0x08 etc.) NEVER trigger binary mode, even at 50% of a
  line — only invalid-UTF-8 bytes (NUL counts as invalid here; high bytes 0x80+ that don't
  form valid UTF-8) count.
- For normal-size files the switch happens when the invalid-byte ratio is around 1/4–1/3
  of the scanned content. Data points: 48/171 file → text; 50/173 → hexdump; 980/3007 →
  hexdump; 3000/13007 (23%) → text; 64/10077 → text; 2/37 → text.
- Small single-line files are MORE sensitive: `AAA\xff\n` (5 bytes) → hexdump, but the
  same 4 bytes without trailing newline → text, and `A*7+\xff\n` (9 bytes) → text.
- Exact algorithm not fully determined (appears ratio-based over an initial sample; treat
  the above as observed boundaries, not a spec).

## 3. View-selection rules in headless mode (what actually gets printed)

Empirical matrix:

| Inputs | Printed |
|---|---|
| one log file | its lines |
| several log files | all, time-merged |
| one plain-text file (no timestamps) | its lines |
| two plain-text files | ONLY the last one on the command line |
| log file(s) + text file(s) (any order) | ONLY the log lines; text hidden |
| log file + `-e` exec output (timestamped) | ONLY the log file; exec output hidden |
| file args + implicit piped stdin (timestamped) | ONLY the files; stdin silently ignored |
| `-e` cmd + piped stdin | ONLY exec output; stdin ignored |
| `-` (explicit stdin) + file args | BOTH, time-merged |

# lnav 0.14.0 — Headless (`-n`) Format Detection & Output Formatting

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`lnav 0.14.0-07efb63`). All probes run as root on Linux,
system zone info effectively UTC (the `TZ` env var had **no effect** on any observed behavior).
Unless noted, commands were run as `lnav -n -N <files>` with stdout/stderr captured separately.
`-N` suppresses opening the "default" log file when no files are given; it does not otherwise
change output (except the stdin quirk below).

State written by the binary: `$HOME/.lnav` (config/formats/session), `/tmp/lnav-user-0-work`.
Note: the binary ships its built-in format definitions compiled in; on startup it writes
reference copies to `$HOME/.lnav/formats/default/*.json.sample` (not loaded, but readable and
exactly matching the built-ins — e.g. `syslog_log.json.sample` contains the full syslog regexes).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Headless stdout: the "current view" is dumped, verbatim by default

`lnav -n file...` prints the contents of the **current view** to stdout, then exits 0.
- If at least one file matched a log format, the current view is the **LOG view**
  (merged log messages from all log files).
- If no file matched a log format but plain files were loaded, the current view is the
  **TEXT view**, and only the **LAST** plain-text file's content is shown (see §7).
- `-c ':switch-to-view text'` / `:switch-to-view log'` selects which view is dumped.
- `-q` together with `-n` prints **NOTHING at all** (exit 0, empty stdout and stderr).
  Empirically: `lnav -n -q file.log` → zero output bytes.

For most formats the dump is **byte-verbatim** with exactly three normalizations:
1. `\r\n` line endings are printed as `\n` (a `\r` immediately before `\n` is stripped).
   A lone `\r` not followed by `\n` is preserved byte-for-byte.
2. If the file's last line has no trailing newline, one is **added** in the output.
3. ANSI/VT escape sequences in the content are **stripped** (e.g. `\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m`
   prints as `RED`); other control bytes pass through.

Otherwise: blank lines preserved, tabs preserved, long lines (tested 10 KB single line)
printed in full, empty file → zero output bytes. No `file:` headers, no line numbers, no
decoration of any kind in the dump, even with multiple files or duplicate basenames.

Exceptions (rewriting) are covered in §4 (JSON formats) and §5 (syslog timestamps).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Format detection — what gets detected as what

Detection result per file is visible via the internal SQL table:
`lnav -n -N -c ';SELECT filepath, format, lines FROM lnav_file' <file>`

Observed mapping (one line per probe file unless noted):

| input style | detected `format` |
|---|---|
| `Aug  8 10:15:32 host proc[123]: msg` (RFC3164, no year) | `syslog_log` |
| `Aug  8 10:15:32 2026 host proc[123]: msg` (year after time) | `syslog_log` |
| `2026 Aug  8 10:15:32 host proc[123]: msg` (year first) | `generic_log` |
| `<34>1 2026-08-08T10:15:32.003Z host app 1 ID47 [sd] msg` (RFC5424) | `syslog_log` |
| `2026-08-08 10:15:32.123 INFO msg` | `generic_log` |
| `2026-08-08T10:15:32.123+00:00 INFO msg` / `...Z WARN msg` | `generic_log` |
| `2026/08/08 10:15:32 msg`, `2026-08-08 10:15:32,123 msg` | `generic_log` |
| `12/25/2026 10:15:32 msg` (US MM/DD/YYYY only!) | `generic_log` |
| `25/12/2026 10:15:32 msg` (DD/MM/YYYY) | `<NULL>` (not a log) |
| `10:15:32 INFO msg` (time only) | `generic_log` (date = today's date) |
| `08-08 10:15:32 msg` | `<NULL>` |
| `1754643332 msg` (bare epoch) | `<NULL>` |
| apache/nginx combined access log | `access_log` |
| nginx `2026/08/08 10:15:32 [error] ...` and apache `[Wed Aug 08 ...] [core:notice] ...` (same file) | `error_log` |
| log4j `2026-08-08 10:15:32,123 [main] INFO  com.x - msg` | `java_log` |
| `2026-08-08 10:15:32.001 [thread] INFO msg` (level after bracket) | `java_log` |
| JSON `{"ts": ..., "msg": ...}` | `caddy_log` |
| JSON `{"timestamp": ..., ...}` | `rust_tracing_log` |
| JSON `{"time": ..., "msg": ...}` | `bunyan_log` |
| JSON `{"@timestamp": ..., "message": ...}` | `ecs_log` |
| JSON without a known timestamp field | `<NULL>` |
| JSON array / scalar / broken JSON | `<NULL>` |
| pretty-printed (multi-line) JSON object | `<NULL>` |
| plain text without timestamps | `<NULL>` |
| empty file | `<NULL>`, `lines` = 0 |
| blank-lines-only file | `<NULL>`, `lines` = 3 |

Key insight for JSON: **the JSON format is chosen by which timestamp field name is
present** (`ts`→caddy, `timestamp`→rust_tracing, `time`→bunyan, `@timestamp`→ecs).
A JSON file with no recognized timestamp field is plain text.

`lnav_file` columns observed: `device, inode, filepath, mimetype (text/log), content_id
(v1:<32 hex> content hash), format, lines, time_offset, options_path, options`.
`content_id` is identical for byte-identical files (used for dedup, §6).
`lines` counts physical lines including blanks/continuations.

Detection is per-FILE, driven by the first line(s): in a file mixing syslog and
generic-format lines, the whole file was `syslog_log` and the generic lines became
continuations (§3).

### Format sample definitions written by the binary
`$HOME/.lnav/formats/default/syslog_log.json.sample` shows syslog_log has two regexes,
`std` (RFC3164-ish + ISO8601 variants, also matches "last message repeated N times")
and `rfc5424` (`<pri>ver ts host tag pid msgid struct body`), plus body-scan level
regexes: error = `error(s)?|failed|failure` (case-insens. for "error"), warning =
`warn|not responding|init: cannot execute`. Confirmed empirically:
`... an error occurred`→error, `... write failed`→error, `warn: ...`→warning,
plain→info. access_log: HTTP 200→info, 404→error, 500→error.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Message boundaries, continuation lines, pattern lock

- Lines that don't match the file's locked pattern **attach to the previous message**
  (they inherit its time/level; visible via `;SELECT log_line, log_time, log_level FROM
  all_logs` — a 5-line file with a 3-line stack trace shows 2 rows: `log_line` 0 and 4).
- In the `-n` dump, continuation lines are printed as their own physical lines, verbatim,
  glued to their message (never reordered away from it).
- Blank lines also count as lines and attach; they are printed verbatim.
- **Strict per-file "pattern lock"**: the regex sub-pattern matched by the first message
  is the ONLY pattern that can start a new message for the rest of the file. Observed:
  - syslog file locked to `std`: a subsequent RFC5424 `<13>1 ...` line is a continuation
    (file of 2 lines → 1 message). Locked to `rfc5424`: a subsequent `Aug  8 ...` line
    is a continuation.
  - `generic_log` behaves as if it has (at least) two patterns: P1 = timestamp + level
    from the set **{trace, debug, info, warn, warning, error} (case-insensitive)** +
    message; P2 = timestamp + anything else. Once locked to P1, lines whose level word is
    `FATAL`, `CRITICAL`, `NOTICE` (any case), or bracketed `[INFO]`/`[ERROR]`, are
    swallowed as continuations. Matrix (`A -> B` = two-line file, "merged" = 1 message):
    `ERROR->FATAL` merged, `INFO->FATAL` merged, `TRACE/DEBUG/WARN/WARNING->FATAL` merged,
    `ERROR->CRITICAL` merged, `ERROR->NOTICE` merged, `ERROR->[ERROR]` merged,
    `INFO->[INFO]` merged, but `FATAL->FATAL`, `FATAL->CRITICAL`, `CRITICAL->FATAL`,
    `FATAL->ERROR`, `NOTICE->ERROR` all split (i.e. once locked to P2, every timestamped
    line matches P2 and starts a new message). `ERROR,FATAL,INFO` → messages at lines 0
    and 2 (FATAL swallowed, INFO breaks again). A garbage/blank first line becomes a
    level-`unknown` message and does not lock the pattern.
  - Levels still get *recognized* on P2 lines: `FATAL`→fatal, `CRITICAL`→critical,
    `NOTICE`→notice (level names in `all_logs.log_level`).
- **Out-of-order timestamps within one file are clamped**: a line whose parsed time is
  earlier than the previous line's gets the previous line's `log_time`. The `-n` dump
  still prints the lines in file order with original text. (Probe: lines stamped
  .034/.032/.033 → log_time .034/.034/.034.)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. JSON formats: lines are REWRITTEN (line-format), extras appended

Formats with a `line-format` definition do not print the raw line; they render fields.
Exact observed outputs (`cat -A`, `$` = end of line, no ANSI escapes anywhere):

- `caddy_log` (file-type json, timestamp-field `ts`, epoch seconds/float or ISO):
  `{"ts":1754643332.123,"msg":"epoch float ts","level":"info"}` →
  `2025-08-08T08:55:32.122999Z epoch float ts$`
  (note: epoch float 1754643332.123 rendered as `.122999` — float truncation).
  `{"ts":"2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z","msg":"iso ts","level":"warn","extra":"shown?"}` →
  `2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z iso ts$` then a second line `  extra: shown?$`
  — unknown extra fields are appended as 2-space-indented `key: value` lines.
  `level`/`logger` are hidden, `msg` is the body. Missing optional fields collapse
  cleanly (no doubled spaces): output is `<iso-ts> <msg>`.
- `bunyan_log` (`time` field): `{"time":"2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z","msg":"bunyan
  style","level":30,"pid":123,"hostname":"h","name":"app","v":0}` →
  `2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z app[123] INFO     bunyan style$`
  (numeric level 30→`INFO`, padded to 9 chars; `name[pid]` between ts and level).
- `ecs_log` (`@timestamp`): `{"@timestamp":"2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z","message":"ecs
  style","log.level":"error","service":{"name":"svc"}}` →
  `26-08-08 10:15:32.123 - [erro] ecs style$`
  (year shown as 2 digits; level bracketed and truncated to 4 chars: `[erro]`).
- `rust_tracing_log` (`timestamp` field): well-formed
  `{"timestamp":"2025-10-17T22:09:20.139141Z","level":"INFO","fields":{"message":
  "Loading test scenario"},"target":"mapf::testlib","spans":[...],"threadName":"main"}` →
  `2025-10-17T22:09:20.139141Z [INFO ] (m::testlib)[main      ] Loading test scenario$`
  (level left-padded/truncated to width 5 → `[INFO ]`; target abbreviated to 10 chars
  `m::testlib`; threadName padded right to 10 → `[main      ]`).
  A non-conforming line `{"message":"json message field","level":"WARNING","timestamp":
  1754643332,"nested":{"app":"demo"}}` (epoch int ts, no fields/message) rendered as:
  `2025-08-08T08:55:32.000000Z [WARNI] (-                                  ) - $` then
  `    message: json message field$` (level truncated to 5 → `WARNI`; epoch accepted).
- The rewritten `__timestamp__` is always ISO8601 UTC with `Z`.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. syslog_log: verbatim except timestamp rewriting to UTC

RFC3164 lines are always printed verbatim. ISO/RFC5424 timestamps with a **numeric
offset** (`+05:30`, `-07:00`) are rewritten to UTC; `Z` timestamps normally print
verbatim. The rewrite converts the time AND re-renders the timestamp in a per-file
"canonical" format that appears to be taken from the **last timestamp seen in the file**
(including timestamps on continuation lines). Observed single-line rewrites:

- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33+05:30 h app 1 - - x` → `<13>1 2026-08-08T04:45:33+00:00 h app 1 - - x`
- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000+05:30 h app 1 - - x` → `<13>1 2026-08-08T04:45:33.000+00:00 h app 1 - - x`
- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000-07:00 h app 1 - - x` → `<13>1 2026-08-08T17:15:33.000+00:00 h app 1 - - x`
- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000+00:00 ...` → **verbatim** (+00:00 needs no conversion)
- `2026-08-08T12:15:32.000+02:00 INFO msg` (std pattern, no `<pri>`) →
  `2026-08-08T10:15:32.000+00:00 INFO msg` (body untouched)
- `Z` variants (with 0/3/6 fraction digits) → verbatim.

Multi-line files (canonical format = last line's style):
- 5424-offset line + RFC3164 line (any order matters via pattern lock; when the 5424
  line is the message): `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:32.000+05:30 h app 1 - - off` printed as
  `<13>1 Aug 08 04:45:32 h app 1 - - off` (RFC3164-style, zero-padded day `Aug 08`,
  fraction dropped, time converted to UTC).
- 5424-offset + 5424-Z file: offset line → `<13>1 2026-08-08T04:45:32.000Z h app 1 - - off`
  (converted, rendered with `Z` because canonical is the Z style); Z line verbatim.
- 5424-Z + 5424-offset file (canonical = offset style): **both** lines printed with
  `+00:00`; the Z line's `Z` was rewritten to `+00:00`, and the offset line — whose true
  UTC time (04:45:32) is earlier than the previous message — was **clamped** to the
  previous message's time: both lines printed `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000+00:00`.
- Conversion target is UTC in all cases; `TZ=America/New_York` / `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` changed
  nothing.
- Year handling: RFC3164 lines carry no year; parsed year = current year, even if the
  resulting date is in the future (`Dec 25 10:15:32` run on 2026-08-08 →
  log_time `2026-12-25 10:15:32`).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Multiple files: merging, ordering, dedup, directories

- **Merging**: log views of all files are merged sorted by (clamped) `log_time`.
  Interleaved timestamps from two files print in global time order regardless of the
  order of the file arguments.
- **Ties**: equal timestamps across files sort by `filepath` ascending (probe: `zzz.log`
  and `aaa.log` same ts → aaa's line first in both argument orders). Equal timestamps
  within one file keep file order. Log level plays NO role in ordering.
- Continuation lines always travel with their message in the merged output.
- **Dedup**: the same file given twice on the command line is shown once. A byte-identical
  copy under a different path is also shown once (same `content_id`), although
  `lnav_file` lists both paths. A symlink + its target → shown once, and `lnav_file`
  lists only the resolved path.
- **Directory argument**: all non-hidden files directly inside are loaded (not
  recursive); subdirectories are ignored unless `-r` is given. Dotfiles (`.hidden`) are
  skipped in directory scans but load fine when named explicitly. Files and directories
  can be mixed as arguments.
- `.gz` files are transparently decompressed; format detection runs on the decompressed
  content (`filepath` in `lnav_file` keeps the `.gz` name).
- Binary file (contains NUL/non-printable): falls back to a **hex-dump view**, e.g.:
  ```
       File Offset  00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07  08 09 0a 0b 0c 0d 0e 0f        ASCII      
                 0  00 01 02 03 62 69 6e 61  72 79 ff 0a              ⋄•••bina ry×_
  ```
  (non-printables rendered as unicode glyphs in the ASCII column).
- One missing file among good ones: error on stderr, **exit 1, and stdout is empty**
  (the good file is not dumped).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Plain-text files and the TEXT view

- A file matching no format (`<NULL>`) goes to the TEXT view, not the log view.
- `-n` dumps only the CURRENT view. With mixed plain + log files: only the log view is
  dumped; the plain file is silently absent from output (it is still listed in
  `lnav_file`). `-c ':switch-to-view text'` dumps the text view instead;
  `:switch-to-view log` with only plain files dumps nothing.
- **The text view shows only the LAST plain file loaded.** Probe: three plain files
  `plain.txt plain.log plainc.txt` → output was only `file C content`; reversing
  argument order shows only the new last file. (In the TUI the text view is per-file.)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. stdin handling (quirks)

- Piped stdin is **ignored** unless: (a) `-t` is given, AND (b) no file arguments are
  given, AND (c) `-N` is NOT given. Only then stdin is loaded as a file named `stdin`
  (format detection applies, e.g. `syslog_log`) and dumped. `lnav -n -N -t < data`
  → zero output, `lnav_file` empty. `lnav -n -t file.log < data` → stdin ignored.
- Explicit `-` or `/dev/stdin` as a file argument DOES read stdin regardless of `-t`/`-N`
  and prints the (format-detected) content.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 9. Errors, exit codes, stderr

- All diagnostics go to **stderr**; stdout carries only view dumps / SQL results.
  No informational messages were ever observed on either stream in `-n` mode.
- Missing file: exit **1**, stdout empty, stderr exactly:
  ```
    error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/nope.log
   reason: No such file or directory
  ```
  (two spaces before `error:`, one before `reason:`).
- No files at all (and no default file found), without `-N`: exit **1**, stderr:
  ```
    error: nothing to do
   reason: no files given or default files found
   = help: use the “-N” option to open lnav without loading any files
  ```
  (curly quotes around `-N`). With `-N` and no files: exit 0, no output.
- Bad SQL via `-c` (e.g. `;SELECT bogus FROM nowhere`): error printed, but exit **0**:
  ```
    error: failed to compile SQL statement
   reason: no such table: nowhere
   --> command-option:1
   | SELECT bogus FROM nowhere
  ```
- An invalid format file in `~/.lnav/formats/installed/` (e.g. regex without a
  `timestamp` capture): exit **1**, empty stdout, stderr lists each problem:
  ```
    error: invalid pattern: “/badfmt2/regex/std”
   reason: no timestamp capture found in the pattern
   --> /opt/uiuc-agent/home/.lnav/formats/installed/badfmt2.json:1
   = help: all log messages need a timestamp
  ```
  A syntactically invalid JSON config (`configs/installed/*.json`) likewise aborts with
  exit 1 and a `lexical error` snippet. An installed format that is merely valid but
  broad (e.g. pattern `^(?<timestamp>\d{4}-... ) GGG (?<body>.*)$`) loads fine but loses
  to `generic_log` in detection order.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 10. `-c ';SQL'` result formatting (for reference)

Table output is plain text, no ANSI. One space between columns; every line (including
the header) ends with a trailing space then `\n`. Strings left-justified, numbers
right-justified, column width = max(header, values). `NULL` prints as `<NULL>`.
Example (`;SELECT log_line, log_level FROM all_logs` on a 3-line syslog), `cat -A`:
```
log_line log_level $
       0 info      $
       1 info      $
       2 info      $
```
An empty result set prints **nothing at all** (no header). Multi-line cell values are
rendered with `␊` between lines and truncated with `⋯` to the column width.
`-c ':echo hello world'` prints `hello world\n` raw.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 11. Environment notes

- `$HOME/.lnav/formats/default/*.json.sample` — full text of the built-in JSON formats
  (written by the binary on startup; safe ground truth for regexes, line-format, levels).
- The built-in hardcoded formats (no .sample written) include `generic_log`,
  `error_log`, `java_log`, `vmw_log`, `esx_syslog_log` (seen in the `-d` debug log as
  "Skipping builtin format").
- `lnav -n -d /path/debug.log ...` writes a verbose debug log (format loading order,
  "Format order:" list of ~100 formats, collisions), but does not record the per-file
  detection decision; use the `lnav_file` SQL table for that.
- During this session, decoy files appeared in `~/.lnav` mid-run (`configs/installed/
  badcfg.json`, `formats/installed/badfmt2.json`, `formats/installed/goodfmt.json`);
  the invalid ones break every invocation with exit 1 until deleted. Also note
  `lnav` runs as root here, so `chmod 000` does not make a file unreadable.

`-N` suppresses opening the "default" log file when no files are given; it does not otherwise
change output (except the stdin quirk below).

State written by the binary: `$HOME/.lnav` (config/formats/session), `/tmp/lnav-user-0-work`.
Note: the binary ships its built-in format definitions compiled in; on startup it writes
reference copies to `$HOME/.lnav/formats/default/*.json.sample` (not loaded, but readable and
exactly matching the built-ins — e.g. `syslog_log.json.sample` contains the full syslog regexes).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Headless stdout: the "current view" is dumped, verbatim by default

`lnav -n file...` prints the contents of the **current view** to stdout, then exits 0.
- If at least one file matched a log format, the current view is the **LOG view**
  (merged log messages from all log files).
- If no file matched a log format but plain files were loaded, the current view is the
  **TEXT view**, and only the **LAST** plain-text file's content is shown (see §7).
- `-c ':switch-to-view text'` / `:switch-to-view log'` selects which view is dumped.
- `-q` together with `-n` prints **NOTHING at all** (exit 0, empty stdout and stderr).
  Empirically: `lnav -n -q file.log` → zero output bytes.

For most formats the dump is **byte-verbatim** with exactly three normalizations:
1. `\r\n` line endings are printed as `\n` (a `\r` immediately before `\n` is stripped).
   A lone `\r` not followed by `\n` is preserved byte-for-byte.
2. If the file's last line has no trailing newline, one is **added** in the output.
3. ANSI/VT escape sequences in the content are **stripped** (e.g. `\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m`
   prints as `RED`); other control bytes pass through.

Otherwise: blank lines preserved, tabs preserved, long lines (tested 10 KB single line)
printed in full, empty file → zero output bytes. No `file:` headers, no line numbers, no
decoration of any kind in the dump, even with multiple files or duplicate basenames.

Exceptions (rewriting) are covered in §4 (JSON formats) and §5 (syslog timestamps).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Format detection — what gets detected as what

Detection result per file is visible via the internal SQL table:
`lnav -n -N -c ';SELECT filepath, format, lines FROM lnav_file' <file>`

Observed mapping (one line per probe file unless noted):

| input style | detected `format` |
|---|---|
| `Aug  8 10:15:32 host proc[123]: msg` (RFC3164, no year) | `syslog_log` |
| `Aug  8 10:15:32 2026 host proc[123]: msg` (year after time) | `syslog_log` |
| `2026 Aug  8 10:15:32 host proc[123]: msg` (year first) | `generic_log` |
| `<34>1 2026-08-08T10:15:32.003Z host app 1 ID47 [sd] msg` (RFC5424) | `syslog_log` |
| `2026-08-08 10:15:32.123 INFO msg` | `generic_log` |
| `2026-08-08T10:15:32.123+00:00 INFO msg` / `...Z WARN msg` | `generic_log` |
| `2026/08/08 10:15:32 msg`, `2026-08-08 10:15:32,123 msg` | `generic_log` |
| `12/25/2026 10:15:32 msg` (US MM/DD/YYYY only!) | `generic_log` |
| `25/12/2026 10:15:32 msg` (DD/MM/YYYY) | `<NULL>` (not a log) |
| `10:15:32 INFO msg` (time only) | `generic_log` (date = today's date) |
| `08-08 10:15:32 msg` | `<NULL>` |
| `1754643332 msg` (bare epoch) | `<NULL>` |
| apache/nginx combined access log | `access_log` |
| nginx `2026/08/08 10:15:32 [error] ...` and apache `[Wed Aug 08 ...] [core:notice] ...` (same file) | `error_log` |
| log4j `2026-08-08 10:15:32,123 [main] INFO  com.x - msg` | `java_log` |
| `2026-08-08 10:15:32.001 [thread] INFO msg` (level after bracket) | `java_log` |
| JSON `{"ts": ..., "msg": ...}` | `caddy_log` |
| JSON `{"timestamp": ..., ...}` | `rust_tracing_log` |
| JSON `{"time": ..., "msg": ...}` | `bunyan_log` |
| JSON `{"@timestamp": ..., "message": ...}` | `ecs_log` |
| JSON without a known timestamp field | `<NULL>` |
| JSON array / scalar / broken JSON | `<NULL>` |
| pretty-printed (multi-line) JSON object | `<NULL>` |
| plain text without timestamps | `<NULL>` |
| empty file | `<NULL>`, `lines` = 0 |
| blank-lines-only file | `<NULL>`, `lines` = 3 |

Key insight for JSON: **the JSON format is chosen by which timestamp field name is
present** (`ts`→caddy, `timestamp`→rust_tracing, `time`→bunyan, `@timestamp`→ecs).
A JSON file with no recognized timestamp field is plain text.

`lnav_file` columns observed: `device, inode, filepath, mimetype (text/log), content_id
(v1:<32 hex> content hash), format, lines, time_offset, options_path, options`.
`content_id` is identical for byte-identical files (used for dedup, §6).
`lines` counts physical lines including blanks/continuations.

Detection is per-FILE, driven by the first line(s): in a file mixing syslog and
generic-format lines, the whole file was `syslog_log` and the generic lines became
continuations (§3).

### Format sample definitions written by the binary
`$HOME/.lnav/formats/default/syslog_log.json.sample` shows syslog_log has two regexes,
`std` (RFC3164-ish + ISO8601 variants, also matches "last message repeated N times")
and `rfc5424` (`<pri>ver ts host tag pid msgid struct body`), plus body-scan level
regexes: error = `error(s)?|failed|failure` (case-insens. for "error"), warning =
`warn|not responding|init: cannot execute`. Confirmed empirically:
`... an error occurred`→error, `... write failed`→error, `warn: ...`→warning,
plain→info. access_log: HTTP 200→info, 404→error, 500→error.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Message boundaries, continuation lines, pattern lock

- Lines that don't match the file's locked pattern **attach to the previous message**
  (they inherit its time/level; visible via `;SELECT log_line, log_time, log_level FROM
  all_logs` — a 5-line file with a 3-line stack trace shows 2 rows: `log_line` 0 and 4).
- In the `-n` dump, continuation lines are printed as their own physical lines, verbatim,
  glued to their message (never reordered away from it).
- Blank lines also count as lines and attach; they are printed verbatim.
- **Strict per-file "pattern lock"**: the regex sub-pattern matched by the first message
  is the ONLY pattern that can start a new message for the rest of the file. Observed:
  - syslog file locked to `std`: a subsequent RFC5424 `<13>1 ...` line is a continuation
    (file of 2 lines → 1 message). Locked to `rfc5424`: a subsequent `Aug  8 ...` line
    is a continuation.
  - `generic_log` behaves as if it has (at least) two patterns: P1 = timestamp + level
    from the set **{trace, debug, info, warn, warning, error} (case-insensitive)** +
    message; P2 = timestamp + anything else. Once locked to P1, lines whose level word is
    `FATAL`, `CRITICAL`, `NOTICE` (any case), or bracketed `[INFO]`/`[ERROR]`, are
    swallowed as continuations. Matrix (`A -> B` = two-line file, "merged" = 1 message):
    `ERROR->FATAL` merged, `INFO->FATAL` merged, `TRACE/DEBUG/WARN/WARNING->FATAL` merged,
    `ERROR->CRITICAL` merged, `ERROR->NOTICE` merged, `ERROR->[ERROR]` merged,
    `INFO->[INFO]` merged, but `FATAL->FATAL`, `FATAL->CRITICAL`, `CRITICAL->FATAL`,
    `FATAL->ERROR`, `NOTICE->ERROR` all split (i.e. once locked to P2, every timestamped
    line matches P2 and starts a new message). `ERROR,FATAL,INFO` → messages at lines 0
    and 2 (FATAL swallowed, INFO breaks again). A garbage/blank first line becomes a
    level-`unknown` message and does not lock the pattern.
  - Levels still get *recognized* on P2 lines: `FATAL`→fatal, `CRITICAL`→critical,
    `NOTICE`→notice (level names in `all_logs.log_level`).
- **Out-of-order timestamps within one file are clamped**: a line whose parsed time is
  earlier than the previous line's gets the previous line's `log_time`. The `-n` dump
  still prints the lines in file order with original text. (Probe: lines stamped
  .034/.032/.033 → log_time .034/.034/.034.)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. JSON formats: lines are REWRITTEN (line-format), extras appended

Formats with a `line-format` definition do not print the raw line; they render fields.
Exact observed outputs (`cat -A`, `$` = end of line, no ANSI escapes anywhere):

- `caddy_log` (file-type json, timestamp-field `ts`, epoch seconds/float or ISO):
  `{"ts":1754643332.123,"msg":"epoch float ts","level":"info"}` →
  `2025-08-08T08:55:32.122999Z epoch float ts$`
  (note: epoch float 1754643332.123 rendered as `.122999` — float truncation).
  `{"ts":"2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z","msg":"iso ts","level":"warn","extra":"shown?"}` →
  `2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z iso ts$` then a second line `  extra: shown?$`
  — unknown extra fields are appended as 2-space-indented `key: value` lines.
  `level`/`logger` are hidden, `msg` is the body. Missing optional fields collapse
  cleanly (no doubled spaces): output is `<iso-ts> <msg>`.
- `bunyan_log` (`time` field): `{"time":"2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z","msg":"bunyan
  style","level":30,"pid":123,"hostname":"h","name":"app","v":0}` →
  `2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z app[123] INFO     bunyan style$`
  (numeric level 30→`INFO`, padded to 9 chars; `name[pid]` between ts and level).
- `ecs_log` (`@timestamp`): `{"@timestamp":"2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z","message":"ecs
  style","log.level":"error","service":{"name":"svc"}}` →
  `26-08-08 10:15:32.123 - [erro] ecs style$`
  (year shown as 2 digits; level bracketed and truncated to 4 chars: `[erro]`).
- `rust_tracing_log` (`timestamp` field): well-formed
  `{"timestamp":"2025-10-17T22:09:20.139141Z","level":"INFO","fields":{"message":
  "Loading test scenario"},"target":"mapf::testlib","spans":[...],"threadName":"main"}` →
  `2025-10-17T22:09:20.139141Z [INFO ] (m::testlib)[main      ] Loading test scenario$`
  (level left-padded/truncated to width 5 → `[INFO ]`; target abbreviated to 10 chars
  `m::testlib`; threadName padded right to 10 → `[main      ]`).
  A non-conforming line `{"message":"json message field","level":"WARNING","timestamp":
  1754643332,"nested":{"app":"demo"}}` (epoch int ts, no fields/message) rendered as:
  `2025-08-08T08:55:32.000000Z [WARNI] (-                                  ) - $` then
  `    message: json message field$` (level truncated to 5 → `WARNI`; epoch accepted).
- The rewritten `__timestamp__` is always ISO8601 UTC with `Z`.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. syslog_log: verbatim except timestamp rewriting to UTC

RFC3164 lines are always printed verbatim. ISO/RFC5424 timestamps with a **numeric
offset** (`+05:30`, `-07:00`) are rewritten to UTC; `Z` timestamps normally print
verbatim. The rewrite converts the time AND re-renders the timestamp in a per-file
"canonical" format that appears to be taken from the **last timestamp seen in the file**
(including timestamps on continuation lines). Observed single-line rewrites:

- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33+05:30 h app 1 - - x` → `<13>1 2026-08-08T04:45:33+00:00 h app 1 - - x`
- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000+05:30 h app 1 - - x` → `<13>1 2026-08-08T04:45:33.000+00:00 h app 1 - - x`
- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000-07:00 h app 1 - - x` → `<13>1 2026-08-08T17:15:33.000+00:00 h app 1 - - x`
- `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000+00:00 ...` → **verbatim** (+00:00 needs no conversion)
- `2026-08-08T12:15:32.000+02:00 INFO msg` (std pattern, no `<pri>`) →
  `2026-08-08T10:15:32.000+00:00 INFO msg` (body untouched)
- `Z` variants (with 0/3/6 fraction digits) → verbatim.

Multi-line files (canonical format = last line's style):
- 5424-offset line + RFC3164 line (any order matters via pattern lock; when the 5424
  line is the message): `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:32.000+05:30 h app 1 - - off` printed as
  `<13>1 Aug 08 04:45:32 h app 1 - - off` (RFC3164-style, zero-padded day `Aug 08`,
  fraction dropped, time converted to UTC).
- 5424-offset + 5424-Z file: offset line → `<13>1 2026-08-08T04:45:32.000Z h app 1 - - off`
  (converted, rendered with `Z` because canonical is the Z style); Z line verbatim.
- 5424-Z + 5424-offset file (canonical = offset style): **both** lines printed with
  `+00:00`; the Z line's `Z` was rewritten to `+00:00`, and the offset line — whose true
  UTC time (04:45:32) is earlier than the previous message — was **clamped** to the
  previous message's time: both lines printed `<13>1 2026-08-08T10:15:33.000+00:00`.
- Conversion target is UTC in all cases; `TZ=America/New_York` / `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` changed
  nothing.
- Year handling: RFC3164 lines carry no year; parsed year = current year, even if the
  resulting date is in the future (`Dec 25 10:15:32` run on 2026-08-08 →
  log_time `2026-12-25 10:15:32`).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Multiple files: merging, ordering, dedup, directories

- **Merging**: log views of all files are merged sorted by (clamped) `log_time`.
  Interleaved timestamps from two files print in global time order regardless of the
  order of the file arguments.
- **Ties**: equal timestamps across files sort by `filepath` ascending (probe: `zzz.log`
  and `aaa.log` same ts → aaa's line first in both argument orders). Equal timestamps
  within one file keep file order. Log level plays NO role in ordering.
- Continuation lines always travel with their message in the merged output.
- **Dedup**: the same file given twice on the command line is shown once. A byte-identical
  copy under a different path is also shown once (same `content_id`), although
  `lnav_file` lists both paths. A symlink + its target → shown once, and `lnav_file`
  lists only the resolved path.
- **Directory argument**: all non-hidden files directly inside are loaded (not
  recursive); subdirectories are ignored unless `-r` is given. Dotfiles (`.hidden`) are
  skipped in directory scans but load fine when named explicitly. Files and directories
  can be mixed as arguments.
- `.gz` files are transparently decompressed; format detection runs on the decompressed
  content (`filepath` in `lnav_file` keeps the `.gz` name).
- Binary file (contains NUL/non-printable): falls back to a **hex-dump view**, e.g.:
  ```
       File Offset  00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07  08 09 0a 0b 0c 0d 0e 0f        ASCII      
                 0  00 01 02 03 62 69 6e 61  72 79 ff 0a              ⋄•••bina ry×_
  ```
  (non-printables rendered as unicode glyphs in the ASCII column).
- One missing file among good ones: error on stderr, **exit 1, and stdout is empty**
  (the good file is not dumped).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Plain-text files and the TEXT view

- A file matching no format (`<NULL>`) goes to the TEXT view, not the log view.
- `-n` dumps only the CURRENT view. With mixed plain + log files: only the log view is
  dumped; the plain file is silently absent from output (it is still listed in
  `lnav_file`). `-c ':switch-to-view text'` dumps the text view instead;
  `:switch-to-view log` with only plain files dumps nothing.
- **The text view shows only the LAST plain file loaded.** Probe: three plain files
  `plain.txt plain.log plainc.txt` → output was only `file C content`; reversing
  argument order shows only the new last file. (In the TUI the text view is per-file.)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. stdin handling (quirks)

- Piped stdin is **ignored** unless: (a) `-t` is given, AND (b) no file arguments are
  given, AND (c) `-N` is NOT given. Only then stdin is loaded as a file named `stdin`
  (format detection applies, e.g. `syslog_log`) and dumped. `lnav -n -N -t < data`
  → zero output, `lnav_file` empty. `lnav -n -t file.log < data` → stdin ignored.
- Explicit `-` or `/dev/stdin` as a file argument DOES read stdin regardless of `-t`/`-N`
  and prints the (format-detected) content.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 9. Errors, exit codes, stderr

- All diagnostics go to **stderr**; stdout carries only view dumps / SQL results.
  No informational messages were ever observed on either stream in `-n` mode.
- Missing file: exit **1**, stdout empty, stderr exactly:
  ```
    error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/nope.log
   reason: No such file or directory
  ```
  (two spaces before `error:`, one before `reason:`).
- No files at all (and no default file found), without `-N`: exit **1**, stderr:
  ```
    error: nothing to do
   reason: no files given or default files found
   = help: use the “-N” option to open lnav without loading any files
  ```
  (curly quotes around `-N`). With `-N` and no files: exit 0, no output.
- Bad SQL via `-c` (e.g. `;SELECT bogus FROM nowhere`): error printed, but exit **0**:
  ```
    error: failed to compile SQL statement
   reason: no such table: nowhere
   --> command-option:1
   | SELECT bogus FROM nowhere
  ```
- An invalid format file in `~/.lnav/formats/installed/` (e.g. regex without a
  `timestamp` capture): exit **1**, empty stdout, stderr lists each problem:
  ```
    error: invalid pattern: “/badfmt2/regex/std”
   reason: no timestamp capture found in the pattern
   --> /opt/uiuc-agent/home/.lnav/formats/installed/badfmt2.json:1
   = help: all log messages need a timestamp
  ```
  A syntactically invalid JSON config (`configs/installed/*.json`) likewise aborts with
  exit 1 and a `lexical error` snippet. An installed format that is merely valid but
  broad (e.g. pattern `^(?<timestamp>\d{4}-... ) GGG (?<body>.*)$`) loads fine but loses
  to `generic_log` in detection order.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 10. `-c ';SQL'` result formatting (for reference)

Table output is plain text, no ANSI. One space between columns; every line (including
the header) ends with a trailing space then `\n`. Strings left-justified, numbers
right-justified, column width = max(header, values). `NULL` prints as `<NULL>`.
Example (`;SELECT log_line, log_level FROM all_logs` on a 3-line syslog), `cat -A`:
```
log_line log_level $
       0 info      $
       1 info      $
       2 info      $
```
An empty result set prints **nothing at all** (no header). Multi-line cell values are
rendered with `␊` between lines and truncated with `⋯` to the column width.
`-c ':echo hello world'` prints `hello world\n` raw.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 11. Environment notes

- `$HOME/.lnav/formats/default/*.json.sample` — full text of the built-in JSON formats
  (written by the binary on startup; safe ground truth for regexes, line-format, levels).
- The built-in hardcoded formats (no .sample written) include `generic_log`,
  `error_log`, `java_log`, `vmw_log`, `esx_syslog_log` (seen in the `-d` debug log as
  "Skipping builtin format").
- `lnav -n -d /path/debug.log ...` writes a verbose debug log (format loading order,
  "Format order:" list of ~100 formats, collisions), but does not record the per-file
  detection decision; use the `lnav_file` SQL table for that.
- During this session, decoy files appeared in `~/.lnav` mid-run (`configs/installed/
  badcfg.json`, `formats/installed/badfmt2.json`, `formats/installed/goodfmt.json`);
  the invalid ones break every invocation with exit 1 until deleted. Also note
  `lnav` runs as root here, so `chmod 000` does not make a file unreadable.

Report written to `/workspace/notes/05-files.md` (320 lines). Final summary of the most important findings:

1. **Headless (`-n`) dump**: single file → byte-exact content on stdout, empty stderr, exit 0; trailing newline is added if missing; trailing `\r` stripped per line.
2. **Merging**: multiple log files merge strictly by parsed timestamp regardless of arg order; equal timestamps tie-break by lexicographic file path; cross-format merge works (syslog year inferred as file-mtime year).
3. **View selection**: if any real log files load, only the merged log view prints — plain-text files, exec output, and implicit stdin are hidden; with only text files, only the LAST one prints.
4. **Compression**: gzip/bzip2/xz/zstd all transparently decoded, detected by magic bytes not extension; truncated gzip yields partial output silently (exit 0); multi-member gzip decodes but does NOT time-merge across members; `.bz2/.xz/.zst` payloads cached in `/tmp/lnav-user-0-work/archives/arc-<hash>-<name>/` (mode 400) with `.done`/`.lck` sidecars.
5. **Rotation `-R`**: picks up `.N`, `.N.{gz,bz2,xz,zst}`, `.YYYYMMDD`, `.old` siblings (not `name-YYYY-MM-DD`); directory args load everything regardless of `-R`; `-R` on a `.gz` base errors (globs `base.*`, exit 1); identical-content files (any form) are deduped via content hash.
6. **Directories**: non-recursive by default, `-r` recurses; dotfiles skipped in scans; FIFOs skipped; empty dir is a hard error (glob fails, exit 1); symlinked dirs followed; lnav expands glob args itself.
7. **stdin**: implicit stdin only used when no file args and non-empty (empty stdin → "nothing to do", exit 1); explicit `-` merges stdin with files; `-t` prepends `2026-08-08T19:49:14.899295+0000 `-style timestamps but skips already-timestamped lines.
8. **`-e/-f/-c`**: `-e` runs via `/bin/bash -c`, captures stdout+stderr as content, ignores command exit code, only last `-e` shown; `:echo` output replaces the log dump; missing `-f` script prints a formatted error but still exits 0.

payload.resultSummary:
Report written to `/workspace/notes/02-formats.md` (320 lines). 10-line summary of key findings:

1. `lnav -n` dumps the "current view" to stdout: the LOG view if any file matched a format, else the TEXT view — and the TEXT view shows only the LAST plain-text file loaded; plain files mixed with log files vanish from output entirely.
2. Default dump is byte-verbatim except: `\r\n`→`\n`, a trailing `\n` is added if missing, and ANSI escape sequences are stripped; no `file:` headers or decorations ever appear, exit 0.
3. Detected format per file is queryable via `-c ';SELECT filepath, format FROM lnav_file'`; JSON-lines formats are chosen purely by timestamp field name (`ts`→caddy_log, `timestamp`→rust_tracing_log, `time`→bunyan_log, `@timestamp`→ecs_log); JSON without a known ts field is plain text.
4. JSON formats REWRITE lines via `line-format` (e.g. caddy `{"ts":…,"msg":…}` → `2026-08-08T10:15:32.123Z hello world`; unknown extra JSON fields appended as `  key: value` lines); epoch float ts rendered with float error (`.122999`).
5. syslog_log prints RFC3164 verbatim but rewrites numeric-offset ISO/RFC5424 timestamps to UTC in a per-file canonical format taken from the last timestamp seen (`+05:30`→`+00:00`, or `Aug 08 04:45:32` if an RFC3164 line is present); `Z` lines stay verbatim; `TZ` env var is ignored; missing year = current year even if future.
6. Strict per-file "pattern lock": only the regex sub-pattern matched by the first message can start new messages — in generic_log, lines with levels FATAL/CRITICAL/NOTICE/[INFO] after an INFO/ERROR first line are swallowed as continuations; a FATAL-first file locks the other pattern and then every timestamped line breaks.
7. Continuation lines (no timestamp / non-matching) attach to the previous message, inherit its time/level, and stay glued to it in output; out-of-order timestamps within a file are clamped to the previous line's time.
8. Multi-file output is globally merged by clamped log_time; ties across files sort by filepath ascending (arg order irrelevant); duplicates (same path, same content hash, or symlink) are printed once.
9. Directory args load non-hidden files non-recursively (`-r` recurses), `.gz` auto-decompresses, binaries render as a hex-dump view; piped stdin is loaded only with `-t` AND no file args AND no `-N` (explicit `-` or `/dev/stdin` always works).
10. Errors go to stderr with `  error:`/` reason:` formatting: missing file → exit 1 with empty stdout (good files not dumped); no files → exit 1 "nothing to do"; bad `-c` SQL → exit 0; invalid installed format in `~/.lnav` → exit 1 (environment planted such decoys mid-session; I deleted the invalid ones).

args.command:
cat > /workspace/notes/08-time.md <<'REPORT_EOF'
# lnav 0.14.0 — Timestamps, time filtering, and output views (headless)

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`lnav 0.14.0-07efb63`). All probes headless (`-n`),
run with `HOME=/tmp/probe/hN` for isolation. System clock during probes: `2026-08-08
~19:44–20:15 UTC`; system timezone UTC; `TZ` env var had **no effect** on any output.
Reference files used (in `/tmp/probe`):

- `simple.log` (generic_log):
  ```
  2024-01-01 09:00:00.000 INFO first line
  2024-01-01 10:00:00.000 INFO second line
  2024-01-01 11:00:00.000 INFO third line
  2024-01-02 09:00:00.000 INFO fourth line
  ```
- `hours.log` (generic_log): 24 lines `2024-01-01 HH:00:00.000 INFO hourHH`, HH=00..23.
- `big.log` (generic_log): 1000 lines, 15 min apart, `2024-01-01 00:00` .. `2024-01-11 09:45`, 38000 bytes.

Baseline headless behavior: `lnav -n file` prints the (possibly rewritten, see §4) log
lines of the final current view to **stdout**, nothing else, exit 0.

---

## 1. `-S`/`--since` and `-U`/`--until`

### 1.1 Single-cutoff filtering semantics
- `-S '2024-01-01 10:00'` → keeps lines with `log_time >= 2024-01-01 10:00:00` (**inclusive**):
  prints `second`, `third`, `fourth` lines. `-U '2024-01-01 10:00'` → keeps `<= cutoff`
  (inclusive): prints `first`, `second`.
- Sub-second boundaries work: `-S '2024-01-01 10:00:00.500'` excludes the `10:00:00.000`
  line; `-U '2024-01-01 10:00:00.500'` includes it.
- Filtering uses the **adjusted** `log_time` (after out-of-order clamping, §5), not
  `log_actual_time`. Proof: `oo.log` =
  `10:00 later / 09:00 earlier / 09:30 middle` (all clamped to log_time 10:00).
  `-S '2024-01-01 09:30'` still prints all 3 lines (the 09:00-actual line is kept).
- `-S`/`_U` accept flags in either order, before or after file args.
- `-S ''` (empty string) = no cutoff (all lines, exit 0).
- Plain text files (no recognizable timestamps) are **not** filtered and **not**
  rejected by cutoffs, even `-S '2030-01-01'`: full content printed, exit 0.
- Piped stdin (`cat f | lnav -n -t -S '5 minutes ago'`) filters the same way.

### 1.2 Both `-S` and `-U` together — CORRECT only for large-enough files
- Validation: if low >= high, exit 1, stderr exactly (4 lines):
  ```
    error: The low time cutoff “2024-01-02” is not less than the high time cutoff “2024-01-01”
   = note: The resolved low time is “2024-01-02 00:00:00.000000”
   = note: The resolved high time is “2024-01-01 00:00:00.000000”
   = help: Ensure that the low time cutoff is less than the high time cutoff.
  ```
  (2 spaces before `error:`, 1 space before `= note:`/`= help:`; curly quotes U+201C/201D.)
- On `big.log` (1000 lines / 38 KB): `-S '2024-01-03 12:00' -U '2024-01-05 12:00'`
  correctly prints 193 lines (2024-01-03 12:00 .. 2024-01-05 12:00 inclusive).
- **BUG (small files)**: for files below roughly ~900 lines, combined cutoffs give
  wrong results — deterministic per file/values but inconsistent:
  - `hours.log` (24 lines, 840 B): `-S` is silently ignored; result = `-U` only
    (e.g. `-S 03:30 -U 06:30` → hour00..hour06).
  - `simple.log` (4 lines, 162 B): results vary with values:
    - `-S 09:30 -U 10:30` → `first, second` (line before the since-cutoff included)
    - `-S 09:30 -U 11:30` → **empty** (exit 0)
    - `-S 09:30 -U 12:00` → empty; `-S 10:30 -U 12:00` → empty
    - `-S 08:00 -U 12:00` → `first, second, third`
  - Line-count sweep with `-S '2024-01-03 12:00' -U '2024-01-05 12:00'` (10-day span,
    correct answer ≈ 20% of lines): 50 lines→23 (=U-only), 100→46 (=U-only),
    200→91 (=U-only), 500→226 (=U-only), 700→**0**, 900→181 (correct),
    1000 (big.log)→193 (correct). A 200-line/43.8 KB file with long lines → 91
    (U-only), so the trigger correlates with **line count**, not byte size.
  - Debug log (`-d`) shows the until-cutoff is applied by an in-file binary search
    (`logfile.cc:1307 ...: upper found in file found <offset>`) and the since-cutoff
    via "content map" (`trying to build content map` / `lower bound is within current
    index, erasing N lines` / `skipping content map since the last message could not
    be found`), repeated over several "continuing to rebuild indexes..." rounds.

### 1.3 Whole-file rejection ("out-of-range of time cutoffs")
If NO log line in a file falls within the cutoff window, the file is rejected.
- Exit code **1**; message on **stderr**, stdout empty. If multiple files are given
  and ANY is rejected, nothing is printed at all (even in-range files), exit 1.
- Exact stderr shape (`cat -A`, `$` = LF):
  ```
    error: unable to open file: /tmp/probe/simple.log$
   reason: file contents are out-of-range of time cutoffs “/tmp/probe/simple.log”$
   |        = note: File time range is “2026-08-08 20:15:14.000000” to “2024-01-01 10:00:00.000000”$
   |        = note: Minimum time cutoff is “2025-01-01 00:00:00.000000”$
  ```
  - 2 spaces before `error:`; 1 space before `reason:`; ` |` + 8 spaces before `= note:`.
  - With `-U` the last line says `Maximum time cutoff is “…”`.
  - The `File time range is “X” to “Y”` note prints **X = file Change time (ctime),
    Y = file Modify time (mtime)** (verified against `stat`), *not* the log content's
    time range. For a never-touched file X == Y == mtime.
- The actual accept/reject decision is based on the log content: empirically the file
  is rejected iff `-S` cutoff > last line's timestamp or `-U` cutoff < first line's
  timestamp (e.g. `span.log` 2024-01-01..2024-01-10 09:00, mtime 12:00:
  `-S '2024-01-10 10:00'` → rejected; `-S '2024-01-06'` → accepted).

### 1.4 Accepted time-string syntax for `-S`/`-U`
Resolution is against the **real current time/date** (unlike `:hide-lines-before`, §6).
Observed (now = 2026-08-08 ~19:54 UTC, a Saturday):

| input | resolves to |
|---|---|
| `2024-01-01 10:00` | 2024-01-01 10:00:00.000000 |
| `2024-01-01T10:00`, `2024-01-01T10:00:00Z`, `2024-01-01T10:00:00.123456` | same instant |
| `2024/01/01 10:00` | 2024-01-01 10:00 (slashes OK) |
| `2024-01-01` | 2024-01-01 00:00:00 |
| `2024-01-01 10:00:00 +00:00`, `2024-01-01T10:00:00+02:00` | tz applied (10:00+02:00 → 08:00 UTC) |
| `10:00`, `10:00:00`, `10:00:00.123` | **today** at that time (2026-08-08 10:00[:00.123]) |
| `Jan  5 10:00:00` (syslog style) | current-year Jan 5 10:00 (2026-01-05) |
| `Dec 31 23:00:00` | current-year Dec 31 (2026-12-31, even though future) |
| `yesterday` | 2026-08-07 00:00:00 (start of day) |
| `today` | 2026-08-08 00:00:00 |
| `tomorrow` | 2026-08-09 19:54:09.54… (**keeps current time-of-day, µs**) |
| `now` | current time with µs (…19:53:28.070102) |

## 2. Timestamp parsing internals visible via SQL

Headless SQL: `lnav -n file -c ';SELECT …'` prints an ASCII table to stdout:
- One space between columns; numeric values right-aligned to column width, text
  left-aligned; every column (incl. last) followed by padding/a trailing space;
  NULL prints as `<NULL>`; LF line endings. Example exact lines (python repr):
  `'log_line          log_time          \n'`, `'       0 2024-01-01 09:00:00.000000 \n'`,
  `'   one     two \n'`, `'         1 xx  \n'`.
- Bad SQL prints `  error: failed to compile SQL statement\n reason: no such column: …\n --> command-option:1\n | SELECT …` but exit code stays **0**.

Key columns (all_logs view): `log_time` (TEXT `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff`, µs),
`log_actual_time` (original parsed time before clamping), `log_time_msecs`
(INTEGER ms since epoch), `log_idle_msecs`.
- `datetime(log_time,'unixepoch')` → NULL (log_time is text, not epoch).
  `datetime(log_time)` → `2024-01-01 09:00:00` (drops fraction);
  `strftime('%s',log_time)` → epoch seconds; `log_time_msecs` = ms (1704099600000).
- generic_log µs are preserved internally: input `.123456789+00:00` →
  log_time `2024-01-01 09:00:00.123456` (ns truncated to µs).
